passage:
"Say 'water' again, Noor. Wah-tar!" Jiten's voice carried down the corridor, and two boys laughed.
Noor's ears burned. "My name is Noor, and it's not funny."
"Relax, it's a joke."
Thomas looked up from the steps, where he was eating his lunch. "It didn't sound like one."
Later, by the water tank, Noor said quietly, "Part of me wants to talk flat, like everyone else."
"Why would you? I like how you say things," said Thomas. "If he keeps doing it, tell Mrs. Bhatt. And sit with us tomorrow, we keep the corner bench." 🙂
Noor nodded slowly. "Okay. If it happens again, I'll tell her on Monday."

qa.q: Which word did Jiten ask Noor to say again?
qa.a: He asked Noor to say 'water' again, mocking the way Noor pronounces it.

qa.q: What was Noor feeling by the water tank, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Noor felt hurt and self-conscious: the burning ears and the wish to talk flat, like everyone else, show the teasing stung.

qa.q: What could Noor do if the teasing keeps going?
qa.a: Noor could tell Mrs. Bhatt, as planned, and keep sitting on the corner bench with people who like how Noor talks. There is no need to change the accent.

qa.q: How might Thomas have seen the moment in the corridor?
qa.a: Thomas thought the remark did not sound like a joke and saw that Noor was hurt, so Thomas offered a seat on the bench and some backup. 🙂

grounding: A classmate teases Noor for the way Noor speaks; Noor is encouraged to keep the accent, tell a teacher if it continues, and sit with people who value Noor.

passage:
Wednesday. They did it again in the lunch line: 'Hum jaayenge, hum khaayenge,' copying the way I talk, Nitin loudest. Everyone laughed. For a month I've been answering in class with one word so nobody hears my accent. Today I noticed I hadn't said a full sentence all day. That felt worse than the teasing. So after sixth period I went to Kulkarni sir and told him it's been every day since August. He wrote down the names and dates I remembered, thanked me for telling him, and spoke to Nitin's group before the last bell. He said if it happens again, come straight to him. Then Aparna from debate club caught me at the gate. 'Join us Friday. You argue better than half the team, accent and all.' I laughed out loud for the first time in weeks. Maybe I don't have to shrink.
- Vishal

qa.q: What did the group copy in the lunch line?
qa.a: The way Vishal talks: 'Hum jaayenge, hum khaayenge'.

qa.q: How was Vishal feeling after noticing no full sentence had been spoken all day?
qa.a: Vishal felt worse than during the teasing, sad and ashamed at having shrunk so much.

qa.q: Which step helped Vishal most, and why?
qa.a: Telling Kulkarni sir with names and dates, because the teacher acted the same day and offered to step in again.

qa.q: How does Aparna see Vishal's way of speaking?
qa.a: Aparna values Vishal's arguments and treats the accent as no problem at all, just part of who Vishal is.

grounding: A diary showing a teen teased for an accent who stops shrinking, tells a teacher and finds a club that values them as they are.

passage:
Eshaan: they did the walk again today. the swishy one. in front of the whole corridor
Vijay: Manav's lot? I heard. that's so lame
Eshaan: maybe I should just walk differently. talk lower. quit dance club
Vijay: nope. you'd be shrinking for people who don't even like you
Eshaan: easy for you to say
Vijay: true. but dance club thinks you're the best in the group. those are your people
Eshaan: that's actually true
Vijay: and this is like the fifth time. tell Ma'am
Eshaan: emailing Mrs Rao now
Twenty minutes later:
Eshaan: she replied!! she said thank you for telling me, it's not ok, she's talking to Manav and his friends tomorrow morning and she's calling my dad tonight
Vijay: good. walk how you walk
Eshaan: see you at dance club

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling when thinking about walking differently?
qa.a: Eshaan felt hurt and embarrassed, ready to shrink and even quit dance club to stop the mocking.

qa.q: What did Vijay's advice get right?
qa.a: It said not to shrink, pointed to the dance club as real friends, and pushed Eshaan to tell a teacher since it kept happening.

qa.q: How does Mrs Rao see the corridor mocking?
qa.a: She sees it as not okay and acts fast, planning to talk to Manav's group and calling home that night.

grounding: Shows a teen mocked for their manner who is encouraged not to shrink, tells a teacher when it continues, and leans on people who value them.
